title: Sizes, regions and hardware
standfirst: A size is a bundle of CPU, memory and disk, and the bundle decides what you can run. A region decides how far away it is and whose laws it sits under. Neither is as flexible as the word “cloud” suggests.
idea: There are two ways to buy a machine. A fixed menu gives you four or five shapes and nothing else; a configurable machine lets you pick vCPU, memory and disk within bounds. A fixed menu is easier to price and compare. A configurable one lets you match the workload, and makes it harder to know what you are paying for.

The second variable is what the size includes. Disk is sometimes a fixed part of the shape, sometimes an allowance you can exceed, and sometimes ephemeral storage that disappears with the session. CPU is sometimes shared, sometimes reserved. Memory is sometimes the billing dimension and sometimes just a ceiling.
Regions are the least negotiable part. A provider with one region is not a global product, and a provider that offers a region may still store backups or control-plane data somewhere else.

splits.heading: Fixed menus versus configurable machines
body: Boat, Sandboxer, Lizard and boxd sell four or three fixed shapes. Sprites sells one: 8 vCPU and 100 GB, with memory assigned automatically. E2B, Vercel, Runtime and Morph let you choose resources within bounds; Blaxel sizes CPU from memory, and InstaBox sells fixed vCPU/RAM pairs by plan.

The difference matters most when your workload is lopsided. A browser agent needs memory more than cores; a compiler needs the reverse. On a fixed menu you buy the nearest shape and pay for what you do not use.

splits.heading: Disk is part of the shape, or it is not
body: Boat attaches 51 GB to its smallest three sizes and 111 or 251 GB to the larger ones. boxd gives every machine 100 GB and does not let you choose. Vercel gives 64 GB of ephemeral NVMe. E2B includes 10 GiB on Hobby and 20 GiB on Pro, and asks you to contact support beyond that.
Where disk is a separate meter, the capacity you see is not the storage you pay for: Vercel's drives bill on logical used size, and boxd's disk bills on bytes written.

splits.heading: Regions and hardware
body: Vercel is the outlier with 19 regions. E2B and Blaxel list four, Sandboxer and Lizard two, Agent 37 three, and Runtime one. Boat and boxd are EU-only; InstaBox publishes no region selector and its terms say the United States. Sprites does not let you choose a region: placement is automatic near you, according to a community answer.

No provider in this set publishes a GPU for sandboxes. Several say so explicitly: E2B, Boat, Lizard and Sprites. ARM is not offered either, and only Runtime, Sandboxer, Morph and Vercel document nested virtualisation or /dev/kvm. Morph publishes no region or GPU statement at all.

watchFor: The vCPU ceiling: Agent 37's default type stops at 4, E2B at 8, Vercel at 32 on Enterprise.
Whether disk is included, capped or ephemeral, and whether it bills on capacity or on written bytes.
Shared versus reserved CPU: a shared 4 vCPU is not four cores.
Region choice versus data residency: backups and control-plane data may sit elsewhere.
GPU is not available anywhere here, whatever a workload page implies.

rows.scenario: Four shapes cap at 4 vCPU; the EU and India regions need the 2.5× vm type.
rows.note: Four shapes with a 4 vCPU ceiling on the default type, 2–80 GB of disk by shape, and three regions. EU and India require the 2.5× vm type.

source.quote: 4 vCPU is the ceiling on every instance type.

rows.scenario: CPU follows memory: 16 GB buys 6 cores, and anything larger is a custom deployment.
rows.note: Memory drives CPU: 8 GB gets 4 cores and 16 GB gets 6. Custom deployments go to 256 GB. Four regions, no published GPU.

source.quote: a sandbox with 8 GB memory is allocated 4 CPU cores, while one with 16 GB memory is allocated 6 CPU cores.

rows.scenario: Only four fixed shapes, largest 16 vCPU / 32 GB / 251 GB, all in Germany, Finland or France with no region choice.
rows.note: Four fixed sizes from 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 51 GB to 16 vCPU / 32 GB / 251 GB. No custom size, no extra disk, EU-only, no region choice.

rows.scenario: The ceiling is 8 vCPU / 32 GiB, on German bare metal; a US region is announced but not open.
rows.note: Four sizes from 1 vCPU / 4 GiB to 8 / 32, all with a fixed 100 GB disk. One EU region, no GPU, no ARM.

source.quote: This is the largest size a single machine may have, 8 vCPU / 32 GiB unless the boxd team raised it for your org.

rows.scenario: 16 GB of memory does not fit: the ceiling is 12 GiB, disk stops at 20 GB, and the sandbox cannot be pinned to the EU.
rows.note: Six presets from `lite` to `standard-4`; custom sizes are capped at 4 vCPU / 12 GiB / 20 GB with at least 3 GiB of memory per vCPU. No GPU, `linux/amd64` only, and placement is chosen by Cloudflare near the request.

rows.scenario: 16 GB of memory does not fit: the ceiling is 4 vCPU / 8 GiB, disk stops at 10 GiB, and `us` or `eu` are the only regions.
rows.note: Default 1 vCPU / 1 GB / 3 GiB; the organisation ceiling is 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 10 GiB, with `daytona-large` at 4/8/10. Windows presets reach 4/16/50 and GPU sandboxes attach up to 8 GPUs. Two shared regions, `us` and `eu`.

source.quote: Organizations get a maximum sandbox resource limit of **4 vCPUs**, **8GB RAM**, and **10GB disk**.

rows.scenario: Memory tops out at 8 GiB, so a 16 GB workload does not fit at any price.
rows.note: Up to 8 vCPU and 8 GiB, with 10 GiB of disk on Hobby and 20 GiB on Pro. Four regions, no GPU on any plan.

rows.scenario: Fixed pairs by plan, up to 32 vCPU / 64 GiB on Team, with one 20 GiB disk that grows live.
rows.note: Fixed vCPU/RAM pairs by plan, from 2/4 to 32/64, one 20 GiB disk that grows live. No published region selector; the terms say the United States.

rows.scenario: Large is 8 vCPU / 16 GB / 50 GB, and there is no 2-core 16 GB shape in between.
rows.note: Three fixed sizes: Small 2/4/5 GB, Medium 4/8/20 GB, Large 8/16/50 GB. Two regions, no GPU, no live resize.

rows.scenario: No fixed menu: you ask for 1 core and 16 GiB and Modal schedules it, paying 1.15× to pin a broad region or 1.75× for a narrow one.
rows.note: Fractional physical cores (1 core = 2 vCPUs as documented) and MiB of memory, default 0.125 core / 128 MiB. Disk is a fixed 512 GiB. The maximum shape is unpublished. Regions are selectable at 1.15× broad and 1.75× narrow.

source.quote: The cpu parameter specifies physical CPU cores (1 core = 2 vCPUs), and memory specifies MiB

rows.scenario: vCPU, memory and disk are chosen at creation, so the shape can be exact; the ceiling and the regions are not published.
rows.note: vCPU, memory and disk are chosen at creation, with no fixed catalogue. Maximum CPU, RAM and disk per VM, GPU availability, architecture, host locations and selectable regions are not published.

rows.scenario: Any combination inside 16 vCPU and 64 GiB, so 2 vCPU / 16 GB is exact, in one Virginia region.
rows.note: Any vCPU, memory and disk combination inside 16 vCPU, 64 GiB and 400 GiB. One region in Virginia; shared CPU by default, reserved on request.

source.quote: At least 128; at most 65,536 (64 GiB) on a paid sandbox, 4,096 without credit

rows.scenario: The xlarge shape is 16 vCPU / 32 GB / 251 GB, with shared vCPU and reserved RAM.
rows.note: Four fixed sizes from 2/4/12 GB to 16/32/251 GB, shared vCPU with reserved RAM. Two regions, no GPU, no ARM.

rows.scenario: One shape, 8 vCPU and a 100 GB storage ceiling, with memory assigned automatically and no region choice.
rows.note: One shape: 8 vCPUs and 100 GB of storage, with memory assigned and autoscaled. GPU is explicitly not offered; region selection is unavailable and placement is automatic; CPU architecture is not published.

rows.scenario: Even vCPU counts up to 32, 2 GB of memory per vCPU, so 16 GB means 8 vCPU, in any of 19 regions.
rows.note: 1 or even numbers of vCPUs from 2 to 32 by plan, 2 GB of memory per vCPU, 64 GB of ephemeral NVMe, and 19 regions. No GPU published.

source.quote: Vercel Sandbox is available in 19 regions. The default region is `iad1`.

rows.scenario: Pro reaches 16 vCPU / 64 GiB with a 100 GB root disk, but RAM must stay between 1 and 8 GB per vCPU and no region can be chosen.
rows.note: Ceilings by plan: Free 1 vCPU / 1 GB / 10 GB, Usage Credits 4 / 16 / 100, Pro 16 / 64 / 100, Enterprise custom. Memory is 1–8 GB per vCPU and disk is 10–100 GB, growth-only. No region selector is published: the docs claim EU data residency, and BYOC puts sandboxes in your own AWS region.

source.quote: Up to 16 vCPU · 64 GB RAM · 100 GB disk · snapshot + resume

rows.scenario: Memory-Optimized 2 vCPU / 16 GiB fits the lopsided request exactly, in Amsterdam or Frankfurt, for $84 a month.
rows.note: 31 bundled shapes across five families, from 512 MiB to 256 GiB, plus v5 sizing in four US datacenters. Sixteen datacenters, two of them in the EU. Resizing needs a power-off and the disk can never shrink.

scenario.title: A lopsided shape, in the EU
scenario.setup: A browser agent needs 2 vCPU and 16 GB of memory, plus 20 GB of disk, and the data has to stay in the EU. Most providers sell CPU and memory in a fixed ratio, so the request fits almost nowhere as asked.

beats.what: 2 vCPU, 16 GB, 20 GB disk, EU region. A browser workload is memory-heavy, so the usual 1:2 or 1:4 ratio overbuys cores.
On a fixed menu the nearest shape is priced as a whole, so the extra cores are paid for and unused.
Region choice decides whether the machine can run where the data must stay.

scenario.turn: The menu, not the hourly rate, decides the bill here. A configurable provider sells exactly 2 vCPU and 16 GB; a fixed menu sells 8 vCPU to get the same memory, and an EU-only provider may have no region to choose at all.

questions: What is the largest single machine on my plan, and is the top size self-serve or a sales conversation?
Is disk part of the shape or a separate meter, and does it bill on capacity, written bytes or used bytes?
Is CPU shared or reserved, and what does a shared 4 vCPU actually guarantee?
Which region will the machine run in, and where are backups and control-plane data stored?
Can I get a GPU or an ARM machine, or is that a different product I would have to buy separately?
